title: Primitives rollforward playbook and output contracts
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a practical rollforward (non-blocking upgrade) strategy for our Terraform primitives (VPC, IAM, Kubernetes clusters: EKS/GKE/AKS). It standardizes variable/output contracts, minimal breaking-change rules, state migration patterns, and CI gating so module upgrades are predictable for private deployments (VPC and on-prem).

Scope:
- Focus on primitive-level modules used by private deployments: networking (VPC/subnets/route tables), identity (IAM roles/policies/service accounts), and cluster primitives (EKS/GKE/AKS base cluster + nodepool abstractions).
- Excludes higher-level application modules and ephemeral infra (buildkite runners, ci workers).
- Intended for teams consuming modules and module owners.

Principles:
- Backwards-compatible by default: modules should avoid renaming or removing outputs/variables without a deprecation cycle.
- Small, documented surface changes: each PR must include an explicit contract diff (variables/outputs added/deprecated).
- Rollforward (preferred) vs rollback: adopt techniques that allow forward migration of state and resources when safe; rollback is last resort.
- Explicit state transformation steps: no implicit provider state moves during upgrades.

Module Surface Guidelines (inputs & outputs):
- Inputs: prefer explicit, namespaced variables. Pattern: <component>_<purpose> (e.g., vpc_cidr, cluster_master_sg_id). Avoid ambiguities like "cidr".
- Booleans default to false unless opt-in is safe.
- Use object/map types for extensible configs (e.g., map(string) for tags, object({name=string, size=number}) for nodepool).
- Outputs: provide a concise, machine-friendly contract. Outputs must include a json-safe map for primary resource identifiers.

Minimal recommended outputs (module-level):
- id: unique resource id for module (string)
- primary_subnets: list(string) or map(role -> list)
- route_table_ids: list(string)
- iam_role_arns: map(role -> string)
- cluster_endpoint: string
- cluster_ca_cert: string (base64)
- kubeconfig_raw: string (if generating) - encourage consumers to use remote state data source instead for production

Example output contract (VPC primitive):
- vpc_id: string
- subnets: map(string -> list(string))  // e.g. { "public" = [subnet-1, subnet-2], "private" = [...] }
- subnet_cidrs: map(string -> list(string))
- route_tables: map(string -> list(string))
- core_tags: map(string -> string)

Naming / Versioning Convention:
- Module semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. MAJOR when outputs/inputs removed or renamed in incompatible way.
- Tag releases in git with semver and reference in CI.
- Module directory should contain CHANGELOG.md with required upgrade notes for major releases.

Compatibility & Deprecation Policy:
- Additive changes (new variables/outputs) are MINOR or PATCH depending on risk.
- Mark variables/outputs deprecated for at least two release cycles (or 60 days, whichever is longer) before removal in next MAJOR.
- When deprecating, keep old outputs/vars and create new ones with clear mapping. Document migration steps and provide automated tfstate migration scripts when applicable.

State Migration Patterns (common cases):
1) Renaming an output
   - Add new output that mirrors old value (i.e., new_output = old_output).
   - Create a migration helper: script using terraform state mv to move resource addresses only if consumer plans indicate absence.
   - Deprecate old output in CHANGELOG and announce.

2) Splitting a module into smaller primitives
   - Align state resources before split: create alias outputs that map to same resource ids.
   - Use terraform state mv to move resources into the new module namespace during upgrade. Provide clear rollforward steps and a pre-check script that runs in CI to assert no ambiguous resources.

3) Provider or resource type upgrade (e.g., EKS add-on changes)
   - Pin provider versions in module to a minimal compatible range.
   - Run integration tests in a canary account with production-like data.

Rollforward Upgrade Plan (step-by-step):
A. PREPARE
  - Read module CHANGELOG and PR notes.
  - Run local plan with the new module pinned in a forked workspace to capture diffs.
  - Run the provided preflight checks (scripts in /scripts/upgrade-precheck).
  - Notify downstream consumers via slack jira tag and create a short ops-runbook.

B. CANARY (non-prod)
  - Apply in a canary workspace that mirrors production network topology.
  - Validate outputs remain available and resource IDs unchanged where required.
  - Smoke test inbound/outbound connectivity, iam bindings, and cluster join flow.

C. STAGED ROLLOUT (prod)
  - Target 10% of clusters/namespaces first (where applicable) or a single tenant.
  - Monitor metrics: control-plane latency, kube-apiserver error rates, infra drift, TF plan diffs.
  - If no regressions in 24–72 hours, continue rollout in incremental batches.

D. FULL CUTOVER
  - Once all batches pass, create a final commit marking upgrade complete.
  - Run post-upgrade verifications (see checklist below).

E. ROLLBACK (last resort)
  - If a critical regression occurs, revert the module version in the consumer's root module and run terraform apply.
  - If state was transformed (state mv), follow reverse state transformation documented in module notes.

Automated Steps & CI Gating:
- Every module PR must run: unit tests (tfsec, tflint), plan-only CI against a set of golden instances, and integration smoke runs in ephemeral accounts for cluster modules.
- For changes touching outputs/inputs, require a changelog entry and a client-compatibility matrix update.
- Merge is blocked until two approvers sign off: one module owner and one consumer-owner.

Testing Matrix:
- Unit: static checks + plan-only against HCL examples.
- Integration: create/destroy flow for minimal footprint deployment (nightly).
- Upgrade test: previous-stable -> candidate upgrade path applied in test harness (weekly).

On-prem / Air-gapped considerations:
- Avoid generating credentials/CA secrets in module outputs that must not leave the site. Prefer IDs and let site-local tooling emit artifact secrets.
- Include a 'local_mode' boolean to toggle behavior (e.g., do not create IAM roles that require cloud-managed services).
- Provide documentation snippets for on-prem Terraform backends (consul/remote) and required network ACLs for the control plane.

APIs & Consumer Contracts:
- Encourage consumers to reference module outputs via remote state data sources rather than copying generated artifacts into their code. Example: data "terraform_remote_state" "vpc" { backend = "s3" config = {...}}
- Provide an examples/consumer/ directory with minimal integration examples per cloud and an on-prem variant.

Observability & Post-upgrade Checks (must be automated):
- Network: BGP/route-table sanity, NAT connectivity, private->public egress checks.
- IAM: validate role ARNs resolve and assume-role works for the intended principal.
- Cluster: node registration rate, kubelet logs for errors, kube-system pod readiness, and kube-apiserver latency.
- TF: no drift in a subsequent plan; terraform plan must be empty after upgrade (except intentional deprecations).

Checklist (pre-apply):
- [ ] Changelog entry present and linked to PR.
- [ ] Migration script included for any state moves.
- [ ] Preflight checks pass in CI.
- [ ] Canary workspace applied and validated.
- [ ] Consumers notified and a rollback plan documented.

Common pitfalls & mitigations:
- Breaking output rename: mitigation = add shim output and deprecate gradually.
- Deleted resource address: mitigation = state mv with explicit mapping and dry-run.
- Implicit dependency reorder causing recreate: mitigation = explicit depends_on or intermediate outputs.

Operational notes for module authors:
- Keep module examples minimal and always include an "upgrade-notes.md" section in the module root for the last 3 releases.
- Provide helper scripts under scripts/ for state inspection and migration (idempotent).
- When introducing optional features (e.g., IPv6, custom CNI), gate them behind feature flags and default to disabled.

FAQ (short):
Q: When is a MAJOR release allowed?
A: Only when there is no viable backwards-compatible mapping for outputs/inputs and after 60 days of deprecation notice.

Q: Who approves breaking changes?
A: Module owner + at least one downstream consumer owner + infra-platform lead.

Appendix: quick tfstate move example (documentation snippet):
# Move resource from old module path to new module path
terraform state mv module.old_vpc.aws_vpc.main module.new_vpc.aws_vpc.main

Closing notes:
This playbook is a practical, ops-oriented binder for how we design, evolve, and rollforward primitive modules with minimal customer disruption. It's intentionally prescriptive where we've observed repeated incidents (state moves, missing outputs, on-prem gotchas). Next steps: publish to Confluence, wire preflight scripts into the module template, and run a tabletop exercise for a sample EKS primitive upgrade.
